subject: mt-info
title: MT.INFO.------CULT.SOLD.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-32 (Spectacle-Diversion Syndrome, Level One) accompanying Braxton's structural verdict on the sixties: 'these people were no more equipped to deal with the transition which took place in the sixties than their parents were … nothing had changed anyway.' MT-INFO (multi-information) is crossed with CULT-SOLD (culture solidification): the question is what multi-information produces when crossed with culture-solidification — the structural failure of the sixties being precisely that multi-information arrived but no culture-solidification followed. FUND-P (fundamental particulars) and SCI-DYM (scientific dynamics) feed downward into the upper-center. DYM-F (dynamics fundamentals) sits between the upstreams and the crossing line. DYM-SPT (dynamics-spectacle) feeds in from the right. AF-TD (affinity-tendencies) and VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) form the lower-left upstream chain. PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics) anchors the lower-center. VT-PT (vibrational point) hangs on the right margin of CULT-SOLD. Structural argument: multi-information is fed by fundamental-particulars and scientific-dynamics from above and by affinity-tendencies plus vibrational-dynamics from below — a doubled upstream consistent with Braxton's decentralization principle. But the crossing with culture-solidification routes through projectional-dynamics, exposing the structural reason culture failed to solidify in the sixties: projection mediated everything, and projectional-dynamics cannot itself solidify. The diagram is Braxton's argument that the sixties produced multi-information without producing culture, because the productive output collapsed into projection rather than solidification.
